properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's idea, 2026-09-01, in his own words: "if a user typed /help link-ideas, for instance, it would be cool if that showed them an expanded version of link-ideas and maybe some simple examples of how to use them."

⭐ AND THE SENTENCE THAT CAME WITH IT IS THE MORE IMPORTANT HALF: **"I developed this, but I don't even know how to use most of them (I usually let the agent use them)."**

That is the author of reflow2 saying he is not a user of his own command surface. It reframes what `/help <command>` would be FOR: not onboarding a stranger, but giving a person who owns the design a way to use it DIRECTLY rather than only through an agent. Those are different products. The existing `help` skill is written for the first and would not serve the second — its own honest-limits section says it explains the TOOL and cannot explain a design.

WHAT AN EXPANSION WOULD CARRY, unresolved:
· the skill's own trigger — WHEN to reach for it — which is already the first sentence of every description
· a worked example: what the user types, and what comes back
· what it will NOT do, which the `help` skill already argues is the section a skeptical reader trusts most
· whether it answers for the 3 TOOL-BACKED commands (`/debt`, `/decisions`, `/next`) too, which have no skill to expand

WHERE THE CONTENT WOULD COME FROM, and this is the real question. Three candidates, none chosen:
① THE SKILL BODY ITSELF, already served in full by `get_skill`. Free, always in step with the running version — and written for an AGENT to follow, not for a person to read. A user typing `/help link-ideas` would get a procedure aimed at somebody else.
② A NEW `examples` SECTION IN EACH SKILL.md. Honest and versioned with the skill; 25 sections to write, and worked examples go stale in a way trigger prose does not.
③ GENERATED FROM REAL USE — the graph already records sessions, and `dec:how-should-reflow2-log-its-own-usage` is open on exactly whether tool and skill use gets logged. An example drawn from a real session cannot be aspirational. Depends on a decision nobody has taken.

⚠️ THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is Anthony's own standing one: this is reflow2 explaining reflow2, which is the self-absorption he has warned about twice. What rescues it is that the reported user is a REAL user who is blocked — he cannot use two thirds of his own surface — so the need is field evidence rather than polish. But the scope should stay the smallest thing that unblocks a person, not a documentation programme.

📌 NOT THE SAME AS the settled part of the same conversation: `/help` with no argument listing all 28 commands is his instruction and is being built, not brainstormed. This node is only the per-command expansion.
properties.name: OPEN — should `/help <command>` expand one command with worked examples, for a user who has only ever watched an agent use it?
properties.rationale:
Anthony's idea, relayed in his words. The reframing — that the ask is about a user who only ever watched an agent, rather than about a newcomer — is his sentence, not an inference.

The three content sources and the self-absorption counter-argument are this session's, recorded beside the idea rather than used to decide it.
